title: Help
description: Answers to common questions about installing, updates and rollbacks. If yours is not here, collect the logs and write to us.
supportDescription: Send a report right from the manager — the logs are collected for you and personal data is hidden. Or collect a logs archive to the desktop and attach it to a message on the site.

install.question: How do I install the modpack?
install.answer: On Home press “Install the modpack”. The manager finds Mir Tankov through Lesta Game Center, offers the recommended set and shows what will be installed. Press “Install” — if anything fails halfway, the previous files are put back.

notFound.question: The manager did not find the game
notFound.answer: If the game was not installed through Lesta Game Center or lives on another drive, press “Choose a folder…” and pick the client root — the folder with Tanki.exe. Clients older than 1.35 and non-Lesta clients are not supported.

afterPatch.question: What happens after a game update?
afterPatch.answer: After a patch the game looks for mods in a new mods\<version> folder. The manager notices it on its own: it moves the modpack to the new folder or installs a compatible version once it is out. If auto-move is off in Settings, Home shows a “Move” or “Update” button.

notWorking.question: Mods stopped working after a patch
notWorking.answer: Close the game and press “Check now” on Home. If the modpack is up to date and the problem stays, clear the game cache in Settings. If that does not help, open Components: the mods folder check shows conflicts and missing files.

conflicts.question: What is a mod conflict?
conflicts.answer: Another mod that does the same as one of our components (a second MoE calculator, say) or overwrites its files. Together such mods give double panels and errors. The manager only reports conflicts — other mods are removed only when you choose so.

presets.question: How do the ready-made sets differ?
presets.answer: “Recommended” is everything for every day. “Minimal” keeps only light components for slower PCs. “Streamer” is what viewers see on a stream. Any set can be adjusted with the checkboxes — it then becomes “Custom”.

sets.question: How is a set different from a profile?
sets.answer: A set is the list of installed components (“what is installed”). A profile is the component settings from the in-game mod window (“how they look”). Both can be shared with a code.

fairPlay.question: Can I get banned?
fairPlay.answer: The modpack holds only allowed mods: it never shows enemies beyond what the client shows — no positions, no enemy reload timers, no aim hints. Every component carries a “Fair play” note that explains it.

fps.question: Will my FPS drop?
fps.answer: Components carry a load mark: light, medium, heavy. On a slower PC pick the “Minimal” set or turn on “Light only” in Components.

uninstall.question: How do I remove the modpack?
uninstall.answer: Open Settings → “Remove the modpack”. Only our files are removed, other mods stay. You can keep the mod settings in case you come back.

smartscreen.question: Windows warns me on launch
smartscreen.answer: The manager is not signed with a developer certificate yet, so SmartScreen may show a warning. Press “More info” → “Run anyway”. Updates of the manager itself are checked with a digital signature.

tips.home: The essentials at a glance: is the game found, is the modpack installed, are there updates. The manager checks for updates on its own, on the schedule from Settings.
tips.install: Four steps: game, components, other mods, install. If the install fails halfway, the previous files are put back.
tips.components: The switch turns a component on or off without reinstalling. Changes apply on the next game launch.
tips.sets: A set remembers a list of components. “Apply” opens the install wizard with that list — you see the changes before installing.
tips.profiles: A profile keeps the component settings from the in-game mod window. Apply a profile while the game is closed.
